sources.title: Microsoft extends buyouts to 60,000 staff in India, US, UK and Canada
Microsoft offers buyouts to around 60,000 employees to contain costs
Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees as AI leads to efficiency push
Microsoft offers buyouts to around 60,000 employees, reports say

en.title: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees worldwide
en.dek: Microsoft extends buyout offers to staff in India, US, UK, Canada as part of cost containment.
facts: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees across India, the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada.
Eligible employees are at experience level 70 or below and include teams such as AI experiences, Copilot, finance, human resources, Xbox and Windows + Devices.
The offer provides benefits similar to a standard severance package and has no age, tenure or performance criteria.
Employees must decide by early December and will leave on December 31 if they accept.
The program follows 4,800 layoffs announced in July and follows a voluntary retirement program earlier this year.
body: Microsoft announced a voluntary exit offer for up to 60,000 employees in October 2026, according to a memo from Chief People Officer Amy Coleman. The offer applies to staff in India, the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada who are at experience level 70 or below. Employees in teams such as AI experiences, Copilot, finance, human resources, Xbox and Windows + Devices are eligible, while marketing, sales and security teams are excluded.

The buyout package mirrors standard severance and does not consider age, tenure or performance. Employees who accept will receive financial support and career planning resources. The decision deadline is early December, with departures scheduled for December 31.

Microsoft said the program is part of a cost‑containment strategy aimed at balancing AI infrastructure spending with capital efficiency. The company has forecast $175 billion in capital expenditures for 2026 and has been investing heavily in AI data centers and chips. The offer follows a July layoff of 4,800 employees, primarily in Xbox and commercial sales.

The voluntary exit offer is a new approach for Microsoft, building on lessons from a previous voluntary retirement program that targeted about 9,000 U.S. employees. The company stated it may consider future voluntary exit offers where business and workforce needs arise. Microsoft is scheduled to report third‑quarter results later in the week.
en.context: Microsoft is investing heavily in artificial intelligence and related infrastructure, prompting a need to manage costs. The company previously cut 4,800 jobs in July and offered a voluntary retirement program earlier this year.
